sets.title: Law and method changes
sets.what: Changes since 2016 that break year-to-year comparisons.
rows: HB 458 (134th GA, effective 2023-04-07): photo ID to vote in person; ID number or copy for mail ballots; one secure drop box per county, only at the board office; mail-ballot applications due close of business 7 days before Election Day (was noon the Saturday before); postmark grace cut from 10 days to 4; provisional/ID cure window cut from 7 days to 4; in-person absentee voting ends 5 p.m. the Sunday before Election Day (the Monday-before-Election-Day day was eliminated)

Every 2016, 2018, 2020 and 2022 same-day comparison crosses this break: the last week has one fewer early-voting day, mail requests close a week earlier, fewer late-arriving mail ballots count. 2024 and 2026 are on the same early-voting calendar.

SB 293 (136th GA, signed by the Governor, effective 2026-03-20): civilian absentee ballots must be delivered to the board by the close of the polls on Election Day (the 4-day postmark grace period is removed; UOCAVA ballots keep the R.C. 3511.11 window); also adds citizenship-verification roll maintenance and changes provisional-ballot rules

Final 2026 mail counts exclude ballots that would have counted in 2018-2024 if they arrived up to 4 (2024) or 10 (2018-2022) days after Election Day; "outstanding mail" on 11/3 is final in 2026, not before. Grade note: the deadline reading is from the enrolled text with struck language (pdf text layer) [V text / I reading of strike-through].

EAC Policy Survey 2024 (state self-report): no excuse needed for mail; no permanent absentee list; drop boxes allowed; mail-ballot curing allowed (2024 cure deadline 11/9/2024); postmark deadline 11/4/2024 (day before ED); in-person early voting offered; vote centers during early voting only; no same-day registration
Baseline facts for 2024; Ohio has had no-excuse absentee voting since 2006 [I]
Congressional redistricting: Ohio Redistricting Commission adopted a new congressional map in late 2025 for the 2026 election (the 2022 map was only valid for two cycles under Art. XIX)

CD-number comparisons with 2018-2024 are not like-for-like; county comparisons are. The site r6 House table uses 2026 lines for early vote (voter file CD) and 2024 presidential margins re-fit to 2026 lines [R registry]; 2024 same-day early vote by CD exists only on OLD lines (cd_ev.csv flags it).
Issue 3 on the Nov 3, 2026 ballot: legislatively referred constitutional amendment requiring photo ID to vote (enshrines current HB 458 rules)
Turnout driver at most marginal; no change to 2026 voting rules

2026 calendar: registration closed 10/5/2026; in-person absentee 10/6-11/1 (ends 5 p.m. Sunday); first in-person ballots in the SOS file on 10/6 (E-28). 2024: first ballots 10/8/2024 (E-28). Mail ballots must arrive by 7:30 p.m. 11/3.
Same E-n alignment for 2024 and 2026 (both start E-28); 2022 started 10/12 (E-27) and had a Monday-before-ED day [I from HB 458]
late-arriving mail counted (or not): final mail counts and post-ED count timing differ
EAC 2024 survey vs NCSL 2026 table (different instruments: verify statute)
SB 293 (2025): most mail ballots must arrive by close of polls (was postmark + 4 days); UOCAVA keep 4 days
BREAK vs 2018-2024: late-arriving mail no longer counts; mail returns front-load; final mail count lower for the same behavior
